cards.cardName: Uncle FrizzleBob's Kayfabizarro Komik Kult Kards
cards.power: Smashes through the fourth wall to deliver epistemic sabotage directly to the prefrontal cortex.
cards.lore: The truth isn't hidden in textbooks—it's scribbled in the margins by the people they kicked out of the room.
cards.gradeReason: FrizzleBob in full costume — the fourth wall is already rubble before you read the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink comics. Subject: cartoon rabbit bursting through brick wall, textbooks flying. Mood: gleeful chaos.

cards.power: Dictates the mechanics: Cut on the dotted lines, build your deck, and trust no authority.
cards.lore: A game is just a reality you willingly consent to—choose yours carefully.
cards.gradeReason: Explains how to play. Sharp lore but the power is pure instruction, zero performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: instructional diagram, hand-drawn. Subject: giant scissors cutting dotted lines around rule text. Mood: subversive bureaucracy.

cards.power: Forces the player to observe the margins where the real story is hiding.
cards.lore: If you're only looking at the center, you're missing the punchline.
cards.gradeReason: Directs attention rather than inviting embodiment — cerebral but not yet fully performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dense Wimmelwelt illustration. Subject: packed crowd scene, tiny subversive figures in margins. Mood: hidden truths everywhere.

cards.power: Initiates the Human Nature expansion pack, activating all psychology and anthropology discounts.
cards.lore: The ultimate cosmic joke: Being biologically wired for love in a society built for spreadsheets.
cards.gradeReason: Lands instantly — every player at the table has lived this joke and will not recover.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: expressive ink. Subject: bewildered human in business suit surrounded by neurons and spreadsheets. Mood: existential comedy.

cards.power: When played, all players share one example of cooperation, adding [A+1] to the Stage.
cards.lore: Darwin knew cooperation wasn't evolution's enemy, but its main engine—sympathetic communities flourish best.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanic, solid reframe of Darwin mythology — needs the share-an-example beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian naturalist engraving. Subject: Darwin surrounded by cooperating animals, sharing food. Mood: warm revisionism.

cards.power: Merges two cards on the Stage into a single, dominant entity with combined effects.
cards.lore: Life conquered the globe not by combat, but through microscopic networking and cellular fusion.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic is elegant but the card name reads academic — merger action does the embodiment work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scientific illustration, dramatic. Subject: octopus-like scientist merging cellular structures under microscope. Mood: cooperative conquest.

cards.power: Allows you to copy the dice value of a player who helped you; reciprocity becomes your shield.
cards.lore: Even among pure egoists, the mathematical certainty is that Tit for Tat cooperation wins the long game.
cards.gradeReason: Tit for Tat scrawled right on the art — player becomes the strategy before reading the rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hand-scrawled diagram. Subject: fox with mirrored handwritten Tit-for-Tat notes, dice reflected. Mood: calculated cooperation.

cards.power: Synthesizes the board: cancels all active competitive multipliers and resets the baseline to cooperative.
cards.lore: The Alpha Male myth is a statistical rounding error in an otherwise cooperative biosphere.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a precision strike — mechanic is functional and clear but board-reset is abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scientific diagram, arrows. Subject: graph showing combat-to-cooperation shift, micro vs macro scale. Mood: paradigm shift.

cards.power: Mirrors another player's emotion, granting both [A+1]; failing to mirror costs [A-1].
cards.lore: Mirror neurons mean we are biologically designed for social resonance; we literally feel what others feel.
cards.gradeReason: Mirroring mechanic is genuinely performative — held back only by the academic German subtitle density.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist ink. Subject: two elephants facing each other, neural pathways visible between them. Mood: involuntary empathy.

cards.power: Punishes isolation with [F-2], but rewards reconnection immediately with [A+2].
cards.lore: Social pain is real pain—rejection activates the exact same brain regions as physical injury.
cards.gradeReason: Broken-leg / broken-heart diagram clinches it — the lore makes the table go quiet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical diagram, emotional. Subject: brain scan showing rejection pain = physical pain, two EKG lines. Mood: scientific tenderness.

cards.power: Marks a player as isolated, aggressively increasing their Fragility [F+2] every turn until they reconnect.
cards.lore: Chronic loneliness destroys the immune system and acts as a biological hunger signal for connection.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanically the loneliest card in the deck — lore is solid, mechanic does the work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholy ink. Subject: lone penguin in urban setting, biological fragility meter rising. Mood: tender alarm.

cards.power: Reveals hidden emotional states, allowing players to bypass logical defenses for one round.
cards.lore: We are not thinking machines that feel; we are feeling machines that occasionally think.
cards.gradeReason: One of the deck's sharpest lines — the inversion lands as a total worldview flip.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: circuit diagram meets anatomy. Subject: brain wired as rejection sensor feeding pain gland, bypassing logic. Mood: radical empathy.

cards.power: Morality functions automatically this round; trust replaces all dice rolls and calculation.
cards.lore: Morality isn't trained into us by society—toddlers help instinctively before they can even speak.
cards.gradeReason: Toddler-morality insight is Grade 1 material; the mechanic-as-rule-suspension reads too abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: naturalist sketch. Subject: tiny child and chimp sharing food, reaching past bars. Mood: pre-verbal goodness.

cards.power: Sacrifice [A-1] to violently reduce an offender's Rivalry by [R-2]; justice demands a price.
cards.lore: We would rather burn our own resources than let an unfair actor walk away unpunished.
cards.gradeReason: Every player has done this in a boardgame — recognition is instant and slightly uncomfortable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic engraving. Subject: gorilla burning gold coins while staring down an opponent. Mood: righteous spite.

cards.power: Triggers post-conflict reconciliation, restoring [A+2] to both parties and erasing conflict memory.
cards.lore: Empathy, consolation, and justice aren't human inventions; they are ancient evolutionary inheritances.
cards.gradeReason: Reconciliation is clear and warm — lore is correct but lands slightly soft as performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: naturalist compassion. Subject: two chimps in post-fight hug, researcher observing quietly. Mood: ancient warmth.

cards.power: Rebalances the Stage by redistributing hoarded resources equally among all active players.
cards.lore: True justice is a biological reflex, part nurturing hug, part spiteful rejection of the greedy.
cards.gradeReason: Scales diagram is clean, lore has the right voltage — the redistribution mechanic is functional.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: balance diagram. Subject: scales weighing instinctive help vs calculated punishment. Mood: evolutionary justice.

cards.power: Grants [A+2] if you consider others' welfare before your own; penalizes ignorance with [F-1].
cards.lore: The prophet of capitalism actually believed human nature was deeply rooted in empathy; a fact history conveniently forgot.
cards.gradeReason: The misread-prophet twist is a political time bomb — 'history conveniently forgot' lands like a dropped wrench.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage book cover parody. Subject: deer in spectacles holding Wealth of Nations, Theory of Moral Sentiments visible. Mood: ironic vindication.

cards.cardName: Gary Becker – Der Homo Oeconomicus Architekt
cards.power: Turns all actions into transactions; buys cooperation with [R+2], but permanently halves all trust effects.
cards.lore: By reducing all human behavior to a cost-benefit analysis, he built a perfect model of a sociopath.
cards.gradeReason: 'A perfect model of a sociopath' — this is what a knockout line sounds like.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate gothic. Subject: hamster economist with calculator replacing heart, cost-benefit charts everywhere. Mood: clinical horror.

cards.power: Challenges any selfish nature assumption; if debunked, all players gain [A+1] and [F-1].
cards.lore: Most cynical proofs of human evil are fabricated myths—deep down, humanity is aggressively decent.
cards.gradeReason: 'Aggressively decent' is a gem — the mechanic 'challenges' is too passive to fully earn Grade 1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rebellious nonfiction. Subject: journalist dismantling Lord of the Flies myth with evidence files. Mood: optimistic insurgency.

cards.power: Disables all purely transactional or selfish multipliers on the board for three consecutive rounds.
cards.lore: We built an entire global economic system for a species that doesn't actually exist.
cards.gradeReason: The best line in the deck. Full stop. Three-round disable is a bold mechanic that earns it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical diagram. Subject: Homo Oeconomicus autopsy on table — missing heart, social cortex, biological empathy. Mood: deadpan horror.

cards.power: Lose [A-1] to give another [A+2]; if they pay it forward, you reap a massive [F-2] reward.
cards.lore: True altruism exists. We don't just help to feel good; we help because genuine empathy compels action.
cards.gradeReason: Loss-for-gain mechanic is clever but the embodiment invite is carried by the lore, not the card name.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surreal generosity. Subject: dolphin opening treasure chest for others, ripple effect cascading outward. Mood: selfless abundance.

cards.power: The first helpful action in a round automatically succeeds without a dice roll; purity bypasses calculation.
cards.lore: We are born helpers; toddlers will drop everything to assist a stranger without any promise of a reward.
cards.gradeReason: Describes a rule rather than inviting embodiment — weakest performance invitation in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm naturalist sketch. Subject: toddler and puppy instinctively helping fallen bird. Mood: innocent compulsion.

cards.power: Give away a card to trigger your brain's reward center; immediately gain [A+2] and [F-1].
cards.lore: Evolution hardwired generosity to the same neurological pleasure centers as food and sex.
cards.gradeReason: Give-a-card = instant dopamine = perfect mechanical embodiment. Lore closes the loop hard.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neuroscience meets baroque. Subject: glowing brain scan on skull, giving hand radiating reward signals. Mood: biological ecstasy.

cards.power: Any altruistic action taken this round doubles in power and creates a cascading benefit to the next player.
cards.lore: Selflessness isn't a sacrifice; it is the most sophisticated dopamine hack in evolutionary history.
cards.gradeReason: Strong closing line — cascade mechanic is functionally elegant but the loop diagram is abstract.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flow diagram. Subject: see-need-feel empathy-help-brain glows cycle, biological feedback loop. Mood: virtuous cascade.

cards.power: Roll with advantage if acting from genuine interest; roll with disadvantage if bribed.
cards.lore: The Overjustification Effect: paying someone to do what they love is the fastest way to kill their passion.
cards.gradeReason: Advantage-if-genuine / disadvantage-if-bribed is mechanical poetry that forces the player to know themselves.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dual-panel contrast. Subject: raccoon building tower for joy vs raccoon building it for coins, second raccoon slumping. Mood: corrupted passion.

cards.power: If offered a massive reward [R+2], you choke under pressure: roll twice and take the worse result.
cards.lore: The rational market is a joke; huge financial bonuses reliably cause performance-destroying panic.
cards.gradeReason: Choke mechanic is funny and memorable — card name is a mouthful that slows the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: economic satire. Subject: crow with money bag choking at critical moment, two bad dice showing. Mood: performance panic.

cards.power: Monetizing any cooperative action this round degrades all [A] values by 1.
cards.lore: Motivation Crowding Theory: putting a price tag on a civic duty destroys the moral desire to do it.
cards.gradeReason: 'Motivation Crowding Theory' in lore breaks immersion — mechanic is sharper than the academic framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark urban sketch. Subject: panda selling social norm badges on street corner, crowd losing interest. Mood: corrupted civic spirit.

cards.power: Strips all financial and external reward buffs from the Stage, forcing players to rely purely on base stats.
cards.lore: Carrots and sticks are for donkeys; meaning and autonomy are for living beings.
cards.gradeReason: Best SYNTHESIS line after Egoism Autopsy — the strip-buffs mechanic is bold and perfectly matched.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: economics chart on fire. Subject: intrinsic vs extrinsic graph, money line dropping into fire, joy line rising. Mood: liberation economics.

cards.power: Reveals all hidden tech influences for one round; choose to resist [R+1] or tragically comply [A-1].
cards.lore: Surveillance capitalism doesn't want your money—it wants to mine your behavior, predict your future, and sell it.
cards.gradeReason: Resist-or-comply binary is smart game design — the card name is longer than most tweets.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate surveillance aesthetic. Subject: octopus tech-entity in server room, data streams as tentacles. Mood: digital extraction.

cards.power: Every screen-based artifact on the Stage actively increases Fragility [F+1] for all players.
cards.lore: Since 2010, the invisible umbilical cord to our screens has been silently mass-producing loneliness and anxiety.
cards.gradeReason: 'Invisible umbilical cord' is vivid — mechanic is blunt and effective but passive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholy documentary. Subject: giraffe staring into phone, umbilical cord connecting to screen, loneliness meter rising. Mood: silent epidemic.

cards.power: Pushing yourself beyond limits [R+4] causes immediate burnout, draining [F-3].
cards.lore: We are no longer exploited by cruel masters; we are the cheerful, self-optimizing architects of our own burnout.
cards.gradeReason: 'Cheerful, self-optimizing architects of our own burnout' — Byung-Chul Han's entire philosophy in 14 words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hamster-wheel existentialism. Subject: panda in hamster wheel, smiling while burning, self-built cage. Mood: voluntary exhaustion.

cards.power: Traps all players in an algorithmic feedback loop, restricting moves until a Disconnect action is taken.
cards.lore: The modern world is a beautifully designed Skinner box, and we are paying a monthly subscription to stay inside.
cards.gradeReason: 'Paying a monthly subscription to stay inside a Skinner box' — darkest laugh in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: algorithmic diagram. Subject: attention extraction-induce anxiety-sell solution-demand optimization loop, Skinner box aesthetic. Mood: beautiful trap.

cards.power: Reframes any failed roll as learning, banking an [A+2] bonus for your next related action.
cards.lore: The belief that you are unfinished is infinitely more powerful than the belief that you are gifted.
cards.gradeReason: Solid reframe mechanic — concept is slightly overexposed culturally, which dulls the shock edge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: growth metaphor. Subject: elephant teaching cow to build tower, failure blocks becoming steps. Mood: unfinished optimism.

cards.power: Declare a positive expectation about another player; if they believe it, both gain [A+1] and [F-1].
cards.lore: The Pygmalion Effect: Our expectations of others literally alter their reality and capabilities.
cards.gradeReason: Declare-an-expectation is genuinely performative — requires buy-in from two players to fully activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mythic realism. Subject: turtle teacher expecting dragon; dragon emerging from expectation bubble. Mood: self-fulfilling prophecy.

cards.power: Use a past failure token to prevent a current collapse. Learned resilience is the ultimate shield.
cards.lore: Helplessness can be learned, but so can optimism—hope is a muscle that must be violently exercised.
cards.gradeReason: 'Hope is a muscle that must be violently exercised' — this card leaves a bruise.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: liberation sketch. Subject: lion breaking out of old cage frame using past scars as tools. Mood: earned optimism.

cards.power: Notice one missed detail on the Stage to completely reinterpret its meaning, shifting the game context.
cards.lore: Mindfulness isn't meditation; it is the radical, reality-bending power of simply paying attention to the present.
cards.gradeReason: Good closer — the reframe on mindfulness works, but the territory is well-trodden culturally.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: perception shift. Subject: cardboard box seen as cage / fighter jet / cat depending on observer angle. Mood: reality negotiation.

verdict: The Biology of Rebellion runs like a doctoral thesis that wandered into a pub fight and won. Lore writing is operating at ceiling level — 'We built an entire global economic system for a species that doesn't actually exist' earns a mic drop and a slow clap. Named weakness: German subtitles like 'Die Überwachungskapitalismus-Analystin' are doing linguistic powerlifting when they should be doing parkour, and ADD decks need their own cover page, not a recycled Komik Kult welcome spread. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For anyone who suspects the whole system was designed by aliens who'd never met a human being. Biology of Rebellion gives you 36 science-backed cards to prove it.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — Rabbit-through-wall, scissors, full Kayfabizarro energy — strong but it's the standard Komik Kult Kards welcome art.
coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — 'Welcome to the Kult!' works; 'reality is just a corporate psy-op waiting to be vandalized' is an excellent subtitle.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Perfect tonal match for the FrizzleBob universe throughout.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 3 — Follows the established Komik Kult Kards template; no ADD-specific identity.
coverQA.coverViral: 3 — Functions as a welcome/rules spread rather than a viral hook; missing a standalone cover moment.
coverQA.coverNote: The welcome spread delivers on energy — rabbit through drywall, scissors cutting reality, full aesthetic. But as an ADD entry this expansion is wearing the parent deck's jersey. Give Biology of Rebellion its own cover art or at minimum a chapter-zero splash that screams 'the biology has entered the building.'

notes: ADD (add-on/expansion) deck to the 'Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch' series. Structure: 9 pages — page 1 is a 4-card Welcome/Rules intro spread, pages 2–9 are 8 thematic chapter spreads (3 thinker cards + 1 SYNTHESIS diagram each). No dedicated standalone cover page; uses generic 'Welcome to the Kult!' spread. Adam Smith card features prominent book cover typography ('Wealth of Nations / Theory of Moral Sentiments') as an intentional artwork overlay/visual gag — not a font artifact. Cards consistently reference [A]/[F]/[R] stat framework (Agency/Fragility/Rivalry). Chapter headers are uniformly excellent as standalone hooks. Editorial stamps present: 'BLODSINN!' (page 3), 'HUMBUG!' (pages 5, 8), 'KayfaBINGO!' (pages 2, 4) — FrizzleBob commentary layers. Deck traces a coherent arc: evolutionary biology → social pain → fairness → behavioral economics → generosity → motivation → surveillance capitalism → agency recovery. Byung-Chul Han inclusion is a standout — rare philosopher in this deck ecosystem and perfectly placed.
topCards: Gary Becker – Der Homo Oeconomicus Architekt

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE BIOLOGY OF REBELLION – Your Species Is Better Than the Brochure Admits (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Thirty-six scientists walk into a room to perform an autopsy on the most profitable lie of the last century: that you are, underneath it all, a selfish animal.

The lie has a name. Homo Oeconomicus, the rational little hoarder who maximizes himself and trusts nobody, and it got quietly priced into your school, your office, and your feed, because a species that believes it is selfish is a species that is cheap to manage. The evidence says otherwise, and the evidence has receipts. Frans de Waal watched apes reconcile after a fight. Michael Tomasello watched toddlers help each other before they could speak in full sentences. Ernst Fehr put real money on a real table and watched strangers spend their own cut to punish a cheat. Robert Axelrod ran the tournaments where the cutthroat strategies lost and plain reciprocity walked off with the pot. None of it made the brochure, because the brochure is printed by the Extraction Engine, and cooperation is bad for that business.

This is Social Story Wrestling with a reading list. You play a researcher out loud, the table rules on whether the science actually holds, and a century of cooperation evidence has to win its match in front of witnesses instead of dying quietly in a journal nobody outside the field will ever open.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Biology of Rebellion Core Deck: 36 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, each one a real scientist carrying a real finding, featuring Ernst Fehr, Der Fairness-Ökonom, who makes you spend your own standing to punish an offender, Robert Axelrod, Der Spieltheoretiker, who turns reciprocity into armor, and the SYNTHESIS: The Egoism Autopsy, the card that switches off every selfish multiplier on the board at once.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the part where every card can claim anything until the room calls the bluff. Cut on the dotted lines and play the thing.
- The Section Arc: nine chapters that build the case one stage at a time, from Survival of the Friendliest and the Pain of the Pack, through the Homo Oeconomicus Autopsy and the Generous Beast, into the Surveillance Cage that bills you for your own attention, and out the far side at Breaking the Cage, where the deck stops describing the trap and hands you the pencil.

This is the EMBRACE wing of the Hannover triptych, the panel that refuses both the polished rescue and the doom scroll and picks up the pencil instead. Forget hangs on the left, Ignore holds the middle, and this wing sketches the repair from the one blueprint that keeps surviving peer review: each other. The whole triptych lives at protopians.substack.com. Read the evidence out loud, then go be the proof.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Selfishness was never your nature. It was just the cheapest story to sell you. This deck is the peer-reviewed receipt."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
